newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Mobutu says eastern Zaire invaders "devils".
newsitem.headline: Mobutu says eastern Zaire invaders "devils".

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, convalescing in the south of France after cancer treatment, said he had been stabbed in the back during his absence by "devils" invading the east of Zaire.
In a CNN interview broadcast on Thursday Mobutu said:"The whole country is behind me. I am the President of the Republic of Zaire. After my convalescence, I'll return to Zaire as president."
Speaking in French from his home on the Riviera the 66-year-old Mobutu looked thinner but healthy and alert. His eyes sparkled and a smile played on his lips as he parried questions.

"I am fine now, the Lord must love me," said Mobutu a former journalist turned soldier who seized power in 1965 when Zaire, then known as Congo, had been ravaged by five years of civil war after independence from Belgium.
His long rule, during which he has become fabulously rich and the country dirt poor, inspired the coining of the term "kleptocracy".
Zairean rebels, backed by Rwanda, have seized a swathe of eastern Zaire during Mobutu's absence.

He termed the rebels and their supporters "devils" and said:"I have faced a number of problems on several fronts before but this time they stabbed me in the back while I was away. Do you think this would have happened if I were there. No. Never"
Mobutu underwent more than two months of treatment for prostate cancer in Lausanne, Switzerland before leaving on November 4 for the French Riviera.
The Zairean ruler had said he intended to return to Lausanne for a medical check-up but Switzerland has denied him a visa after his presence sparked protests.
In the interview he refused to be drawn on his tactics on eastern Zaire.
"I am a military man, a military leader but I don't want to talk of war or combat.
"I am the longest serving African head of state and my watchword these days is peace. If things get worse in eastern Zaire after I return I can assure you it won't be Zaire's fault," he said.
